name: budget
title: An explicit growth budget in Corbo
description: Collect integers within an explicitly bounded 64 KiB growing-data region; the pool has one vector slot.

name: hello
title: A synchronous entry point
description: `main` is synchronous. Build a package with `package.toml` and `src/main.crb`.

name: numbers
title: Primitives and checked operators
description: Integers default to `i64`, decimal floating-point literals to `f64`. Variables in arithmetic must have compatible types. `as` permits conversions that are exact for every source value; `try_from` is fallible. Integer arithmetic, shifts and indexing retain their checks.

name: control
title: Expressions and control flow
description: Blocks, `if`, `match` and `loop` can produce values. Semicolons distinguish statements from trailing values. `continue` and `break` clean up the scopes they leave.

name: tuples
title: Functions, tuples and destructuring
description: Functions can return tuples of two or more values. Types are inferred by position when no binding annotation is supplied.

name: methods
title: Structs, constants and receiver modes
description: Receiver signatures determine whether a method borrows, mutably borrows or consumes its receiver. Associated constants use `Type::NAME`.

name: enums
title: Enums and pattern matching
description: Variants can carry named or positional payloads. A value match transfers the selected payload according to its ordinary ownership rules.

name: errors
title: Result, Option and early propagation
description: `?` returns the failure/absence from the enclosing function. Result errors of different types require a statically resolved `Outer::from(Inner) -> Outer`; there is no implicit arbitrary conversion.

name: moves
title: Moves and explicit copies
description: Assignment transfers a value. Call `copy` explicitly when retaining a primitive source. A move transfers cleanup responsibility; it does not request that an allocation be relocated.

name: borrows
title: Shared borrows and mutable reborrows
description: References do not transfer cleanup responsibility. Their targets must remain valid, and mutable loans exclude incompatible access until their last use.

name: arrays
title: Fixed arrays, structural repetition and slices
description: An array carries its element count in its type. A borrowed slice carries an address and length. Repetition evaluates the initializer once and requires a structurally replicable value; slices retain bounds and lifetime checks.

name: pools
title: Fixed-capacity pools and allocation handles
description: `Pool<T>::new(n)` reserves fixed slots. `new` returns `A<T>`; the pool must outlive that allocation. Dropping a live allocation releases its slot after cleanup.

name: placement
title: Receivers and placement across scopes
description: A block result has an explicit receiver. The post-AST placement plan follows transfers to their final destination while keeping allocation addresses stable.

name: destruction
title: Destruction before storage release
description: `drop(value)` and scope exit call `drop(&mut self)` once, before field cleanup. Moving the value changes who performs that cleanup. Types without a custom destructor use the default empty destructor.

name: regions
title: Datastack budgets, local regions and page reclamation
description: The global datastack annotation and its properties are optional. `stack_region` supplies a local growing-data budget. `free_pages` requests OS reclamation of complete unused pages after cleanup, distinct from moving a cursor.

name: vector
title: Vectors and extraction
description: The vector descriptor has fixed size; its contiguous payload grows within its region budget. Insertion moves an item into the vector. Extraction transfers it to the receiver.

name: map
title: HashMap lookup, replacement and removal
description: Maps accept integer and boolean keys. Insertion moves its key and value; lookup borrows its key. Remaining values are destroyed with the map, while an extracted value belongs to its receiver.

name: text
title: UTF-8 text and caller-owned bytes
description: `String` owns region-backed UTF-8 bytes; a literal provides a static `&str` view. Byte length differs from character count. Convert to a byte slice explicitly with `as_bytes()`. Both `String` and `&str` provide `split(separator)`: its iterator yields borrowed `&str` pieces, preserving empty pieces without allocating strings.

name: closures
title: Closures and explicit callable passing
description: A closure is a concrete captured object. Parameters are typed and braces are required. `fn(...) -> R`, `&fn(...) -> R` and `&mut fn(...) -> R` distinguish value passing from borrowing. Without `move`, primitive/shared-reference captures copy at creation. Explicit `move` transfers captured bindings; references retain their target dependencies.

name: iter
title: STD iterator pipelines
description: Only `Iter` borrows the source. Each adapter owns the preceding stage. `collect(&mut destination)` consumes the chain and moves its outputs into caller-selected storage.

name: generic
title: Contracts on generic structs
description: Type parameters and their constraints also apply to structs. Concrete instantiation retains the ordinary ownership and borrowing obligations of its fields.

name: contracts
title: Static structural type contracts
description: A `with` contract requires the listed methods and permits additional ones. The compiler resolves the concrete implementation statically; no trait object or dynamic dispatch is introduced.

name: modules
title: Packages, modules, visibility and aliases
description: A package is named in `package.toml`. Files under `src` provide components. `pub`, grouped `use` and `as` control access and local names; dependencies can be pinned through package metadata.

name: target
title: Conditional compilation
description: Target selection happens before import resolution. Excluded branches cannot introduce unavailable imports or collisions. The paired `endif` ends selection; it does not create a runtime scope.

name: async
title: Futures, suspension and execution branches
description: Calling an async function creates an inactive Future and captures its arguments immediately. `yield;` suspends cooperatively; `.await` waits without blocking a poll worker. Synchronous `main` starts an execution and waits through its handle.

name: threads
title: Native threads and captured loans
description: A native execution receives its block captures. The target of a captured reference must remain valid through its use; this example joins before accessing the target again.

name: blocking
title: Blocking work from an async context
description: `spawn_blocking` returns an `AsyncHandle`, awaited inside async code. Blocking `join()` belongs in a synchronous context. The blocking operation runs on a dedicated worker.

name: file
title: Files, errors and caller-provided buffers
description: The caller chooses open mode, permissions and buffer size. Paths in this API are NUL-terminated byte slices. This program creates a file in its working directory, performs I/O and deletes it. Moving or dropping `File` closes its native handle once.

name: buffered
title: Buffered I/O through structural contracts
description: Buffered wrappers borrow the stream and scratch buffer explicitly. Call `flush()` to send pending bytes; destruction discards pending output. This example creates a local file and deletes it after closing it.

name: network
title: Typed network endpoints and datagrams
description: IPv4 address objects are passed to bind/connect. Port zero asks the OS for a local port. This loopback UDP exchange uses caller-provided buffers and no external server; TCP and async APIs are linked below.

name: encoding
title: Hashes and encodings with bounded output
description: The STD has native hashing, crypto, TLS, codecs and platform I/O. APIs that produce variable-length bytes take caller-owned buffers. This example hashes two bytes and hex-encodes the fixed digest without an unbounded allocation.

name: compression
title: Compression with an explicit workspace
description: Compression APIs borrow caller-owned input, output and workspace. The example provides the documented Gzip level-1–9 workspace, round-trips a frame and checks its decoded size through the returned count.

name: foreign
title: Unchecked C, typed operands and native assembly
description: Foreign code belongs inside `@unchecked`. `${name}` binds an existing Corbo operand. Header paths are explicit. `addr` is restricted to the unchecked block, and its address must not escape it. ABI, lifetime and memory correctness inside foreign code remain the developer’s responsibility.

name: bounded_text
title: Inline UTF-8 strings with a compile-time byte maximum
description: String<N> keeps UTF-8 bytes inline; exceeding the bound returns an error before changing the string.

name: binary
title: Binary primitives with explicit endianness
description: The caller provides storage and chooses byte order for every multi-byte read or write.

name: time
title: Monotonic time and blocking deadlines
description: Duration expresses a span; Instant reads a monotonic clock, and Timer waits for a deadline.

name: async_time
title: Async deadline waits
description: Async waits suspend the caller task while an existing blocking worker performs the native wait.

name: async_file
title: Async files by default
description: File operations suspend the caller; modes, permissions and seek origins are shared with the explicit blocking API.
